chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning four who testified against a man for zinā, but they were not deemed upright, he said: “They are to be given the hadd punishment.”

key_terms.بِالزِّنَى: with zinā, meaning unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man accused in the case
key_terms.فَلَمْ يُعَدَّلُوا: they were not validated as upright witnesses
key_terms.يُضْرَبُونَ: they are to be struck or punished

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if four witnesses accuse a man of zinā but are not proven upright?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning four witnesses who testify to zinā but are not established as upright witnesses. In such a case, their testimony is invalid, and they themselves are subject to the hadd punishment for false accusation.
